subtitle: Cipher B is the oscillator pane that goes BELOW your price chart. It plots WaveTrend, money flow, and signal dots. Read together with Cipher A (the on-chart overlay from the previous lesson), it's the most-used confluence stack in modern crypto trading.

blocks.content:
If Cipher A tells you WHAT'S happening on the price chart, Cipher B tells you HOW MUCH momentum is behind it. Three layers stack in one pane:

  • WaveTrend — dual blue wave showing momentum oscillation
  • Money Flow Index (MFI) — green/red ribbon showing buying vs selling pressure
  • VWAP — yellow signed area showing WT1 minus WT2 (the histogram)

On top: green and red dots mark cross events at extremes.

The dominant visual is the WaveTrend (WT) — two lines (WT1 fast, WT2 slow) with the area between them filled blue. The math:

  • Take HLC3 (hi + lo + close ÷ 3)
  • Compute its EMA over 9 bars (channel length)
  • Compute the deviation of HLC3 from that EMA
  • Normalise → WT1
  • WT2 = SMA of WT1 over 3 bars

The result is an oscillator that swings between roughly −80 and +80. The zones:

rows: Strong upward momentum; mean reversion likely

blocks.content:
The MFI in VMC Cipher B is NOT the standard Money Flow Index. It's a custom per-bar buy/sell pressure metric:

raw = (close − open) / (high − low) × 150

MFI = SMA(raw, 60) − 2.5

This gives you a value typically in the ±10 range. Positive = buying pressure has dominated the last 60 bars. Negative = selling pressure has dominated. Coloured green when positive, red when negative.

Watch for MFI flipping sign — when a long-standing negative MFI turns positive, it's often early evidence that the bearish momentum is exhausting.

Mathematically VWAP = WT1 − WT2. It's the gap between the two WaveTrend lines. When VWAP is positive (yellow above zero), WT1 is leading higher — momentum is building up. When negative (yellow below zero), WT1 is leading lower — momentum building down.

The VWAP series is essentially a histogram of WaveTrend's micro-momentum. Use it as a leading indicator of the next WT2 direction change.

blocks.title: Gold Buy (green dot) and Gold Sell (red dot)
blocks.content:
The dots fire on WaveTrend cross events at the extremity zones:

  • Gold Buy (green dot) — WT1 crosses ABOVE WT2 while WT2 < −53. Marks the bottom of a bearish exhaustion.
  • Gold Sell (red dot) — WT1 crosses BELOW WT2 while WT2 > +53. Marks the top of a bullish exhaustion.

These are the standard "crossover at extreme" mean-reversion signals. Historically the highest single-signal accuracy in the Cipher stack.

Cipher B v6 includes pivot-based divergence detection:

  • Bull Divergence — price prints a LOWER low BUT WT2 prints a HIGHER low. Momentum is improving even as price still falls. Often precedes a reversal up.
  • Bear Divergence — price prints a HIGHER high BUT WT2 prints a LOWER high. Momentum is fading even as price still rises. Often precedes a reversal down.

The detection uses 2-bar-left / 2-bar-right pivot confirmation, meaning the divergence is only confirmed 2 bars AFTER the pivot — by design, to avoid false positives.

blocks.title: Stack confluence with Cipher A
blocks.content:
The highest-edge setups are when Cipher A and Cipher B AGREE on the same bar:

  • Cipher A Yellow X + Cipher B Gold Buy + Bull Divergence = textbook bottom (very rare, very strong long)
  • Cipher A Blood Diamond + Cipher B Gold Sell + Bear Divergence = textbook top (very strong short)

When these alignments happen, you'll find the actual best trade entries of the year for any liquid coin.

On 2026-05-27 around 22:50 UTC, FIL printed: WT2 = +74.3 (deep overbought zone), Gold Sell dot fired on the 4H bar, and the MTF EMA verdict was "trend_up_aging" (slope had decayed to +0.13%/7d — losing momentum). Three confluent bearish signals.

A short opened at $1.0453 with SL $1.08 (above 10-touch resistance) and TP $0.95 (25-touch support). 4 hours later, the position closed at $1.0407 for a profit. Single best trade of the night when the rest of the book was being crushed by a broad risk-off move.

That's Cipher B working as designed: deep extremity + crossover signal + macro context = high-edge entry.

blocks.title: Don't fight strong trends
blocks.content: Gold Buy at WT2 = −55 doesn't help you if the MTF EMA verdict is "trend_down_confirmed" with a slope of −5%/week. You're fading a falling knife. The cross-at-extreme works as MEAN REVERSION, which requires that the surrounding regime supports mean reversion (range or aging trend). In a strong sustained trend, the dots fire but the bounce is small and quickly overwhelmed.

blocks.title: Bottom line
blocks.content: Cipher B's WaveTrend tells you WHERE momentum sits (overbought / oversold / neutral). The MFI ribbon tells you which side has been winning. The VWAP histogram tells you the micro-momentum direction. The gold dots mark crossover-at-extreme events. Use them STACKED with Cipher A and the macro filter — never standalone.
